sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Over the past few days, President Trump has endured major setbacks at the ballot box where Republicans lost races across the country.
sentences.zh: 过去几天里，特朗普总统在投票箱前遭遇了重大挫折，共和党人在全国各地的竞选中失利。

sentences.en: At the Supreme Court, which appears poised to strike down his tariffs.
sentences.zh: 在最高法院，看起来他们准备推翻他的关税政策。

sentences.en: And in Congress, whose refusal to end the government shutdown will result in thousands of canceled airline flights beginning on Friday.
sentences.zh: 而在国会，由于拒绝结束政府停摆，将导致周五开始有数千个航班被取消。

sentences.en: Today, I try to make sense of all of that with three of my colleagues,
sentences.zh: 今天，我将与我的三位同事一起梳理这一切，

sentences.en: National Political Correspondent Lisa Lair,
sentences.zh: 国家政治记者丽莎·莱尔，

sentences.en: White House Correspondent Tyler Pager, and Congressional Editor Julie Davis.
sentences.zh: 白宫记者泰勒·佩格，以及国会编辑朱莉·戴维斯。

sentences.en: Friday, November 7th.
sentences.zh: 11月7日，星期五。

sentences.en: So, shall we get started?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们开始吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 行。

sentences.en: Lisa Lair.
sentences.zh: 丽莎·莱尔。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the Roundtable.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到圆桌会议。

sentences.en: Julie Davis, good to see you.
sentences.zh: 朱莉·戴维斯，很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: Great to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Tyler Pager, always a pleasure.
sentences.zh: 泰勒·佩格，总是很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: I want to start this conversation with you all with a very simple question for the three of you.
sentences.zh: 我想以一个非常简单的问题开启我们三位之间的对话。

sentences.en: Has this been the worst week for President Trump in the second term?
sentences.zh: 这是否是特朗普总统第二任期内最糟糕的一周？

sentences.en: I think there's a good case to make yes,
sentences.zh: 我认为有充分的理由说是，

sentences.en: because voters actually weighed in on how he was doing.
sentences.zh: 因为选民们实际上已经对他的表现进行了评价。

sentences.en: And I think we've seen a lot of polling, but it's different when people actually go to the ballot box and register their feelings, and their feelings were overwhelmingly opposed
sentences.zh: 我想我们已经看到了很多民调，但当人们真正走进投票站表达他们的感受时，情况就不同了，而他们的感受是压倒性地反对

sentences.en: to the broader Republican Party at this point.
sentences.zh: 目前更广泛的共和党。

sentences.en: And up until this week,
sentences.zh: 而在本周之前，

sentences.en: President Trump has had remarkable success in pushing forward on a number of fronts.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统在多个方面推进工作都取得了显著成功。

sentences.en: Just politically, as Tyler was saying, he hasn't had much in the way of obstacles in front of him.
sentences.zh: 正如泰勒所说，仅从政治上讲，他面前几乎没有什么障碍。

sentences.en: And we really saw that pivot a lot this week on a lot of different fronts.
sentences.zh: 我们确实看到本周在许多不同方面发生了巨大的转变。

sentences.en: So I think it was a bit of a wake-up call.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是一个警钟。

sentences.en: You've been nodding, Lisa.
sentences.zh: 你一直在点头，丽莎。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think the president learned, and perhaps the country learned, that Democrats can, in fact, still win elections.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为总统，或许还有整个国家，都认识到民主党人实际上仍然可以赢得选举。

sentences.en: This was a party that was pretty demoralized, and they got a huge boost of momentum and energy this past week and showed, I think, the White House
sentences.zh: 这是一个曾经非常士气低落的政党，但在过去的一周里，他们获得了巨大的动力和能量，我认为这向白宫表明，

sentences.en: that there is still an opposition party.
sentences.zh: 反对党依然存在。

sentences.en: So it feels like the three tentpoles of this not-great week for the president is obviously, number one, Tuesday's election.
sentences.zh: 所以感觉总统这糟糕一周的三个支柱显然是，第一，周二的选举。

sentences.en: Perhaps number two, the Supreme Court's profound skepticism of the president's tariff regime.
sentences.zh: 或许第二，最高法院对总统关税制度的深刻怀疑。

sentences.en: And third, what I would describe as the metastasizing impacts of the government shutdown, now officially the longest in American history.
sentences.zh: 第三，我所描述的政府停摆带来的蔓延影响，这现在已正式成为美国历史上最长的一次停摆。

sentences.en: Let's dive deeper into the first one, which is Tuesday night's election.
sentences.zh: 让我们深入探讨第一点，即周二晚上的选举。

sentences.en: We've now had several days, Lisa, to sift through the data in the aftermath of this election.
sentences.zh: 丽莎，选举结束后我们已经有几天时间来梳理数据了。

sentences.en: And what we've discovered is just how meaningfully the victorious Democratic winners, especially the governors,
sentences.zh: 我们发现的是，获胜的民主党赢家，尤其是州长们，在多大程度上有效地

sentences.en: won over Trump voters, voters who voted for Trump just a year ago and made him president.
sentences.zh: 赢得了特朗普选民的支持，这些选民在一年前还投票支持特朗普并让他当选总统。

sentences.en: Yeah, and so one statistic that really stood out to me in this whole thing is that Mikey Sherrill, the Democratic nominee who now is Democratic governor-elect of New Jersey,
sentences.zh: 是的，在这整件事中，有一个统计数据让我印象深刻，那就是迈基·谢里尔，这位民主党候选人现在是新泽西州候任民主党州长，

sentences.en: got more than 300,000 more votes than the Democratic nominee did in the last off-year election like this, which was 2021.
sentences.zh: 她比上次像这样的非大选年（即2021年）的民主党候选人多获得了超过30万张选票。

sentences.en: So not only did she mobilize Democrats, she also got voters who were not previously voting for Democrats, people who voted for President Trump.
sentences.zh: 所以她不仅动员了民主党人，还争取到了以前不投给民主党的人，也就是那些投票给特朗普总统的人。

sentences.en: And in particular, there were looking at Black and Latino voters.
sentences.zh: 特别值得关注的是黑人和拉丁裔选民。

sentences.en: Trump made some real inroads in those communities in 2024.
sentences.zh: 特朗普在2024年确实在这些群体中取得了一些进展。

sentences.en: And what we saw in these elections is some of those voters came back to Democrats, that Trump was in fact like renting.
sentences.zh: 而我们在这些选举中看到的是，其中一些选民回到了民主党阵营，特朗普实际上就像是在“租用”他们。

sentences.en: He didn't own those voters.
sentences.zh: 他并没有真正拥有这些选民。

sentences.en: It's not a permanent coalition.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个永久的联盟。

sentences.en: And for the White House, that's a big blow because that means that people are changing their minds about Trump in a negative way, that they were excited about the president,
sentences.zh: 对于白宫来说，这是一个沉重的打击，因为这意味着人们正在以消极的方式改变对特朗普的看法，他们曾经对总统感到兴奋，

sentences.en: they voted for him, and now they're coming to the polls and saying, well, this isn't really working for us.
sentences.zh: 他们投票给了他，但现在他们来到投票站说，嗯，这对我来说并不奏效。

sentences.en: I'm voting Democrat.
sentences.zh: 我投给民主党。

sentences.en: And just to be very specific, and here I'm going to crib from our colleague Nate Cohn, he found that Hispanic voters in New Jersey, where Mikey Sherrill is now governor-elect,
sentences.zh: 具体来说，这里我要引用我们同事内特·科恩的话，他发现新泽西州的西班牙裔选民，也就是迈基·谢里尔现在当选州长的地方，

sentences.en: that group of voters really swung from Trump to Sherrill.
sentences.zh: 那群选民确实从特朗普转向了谢里尔。

sentences.en: And let me give you the number.
sentences.zh: 让我给你报个数字。

sentences.en: Exit polls found that Sherrill won
sentences.zh: 出口民调显示，谢里尔赢得了

sentences.en: 18% of Trump's Hispanic support in New Jersey.
sentences.zh: 新泽西州18%的特朗普西班牙裔支持者。

sentences.en: That's a pretty big number, wouldn't you say, Tyler?
sentences.zh: 这是一个相当大的数字，你不觉得吗，泰勒？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I think one of the things that Democrats are excited about is that they were able to win over these voters that were a long part of their base
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，我认为民主党人感到兴奋的一点是，他们能够赢得这些长期以来属于他们基本盘，

sentences.en: and had been slipping away.
sentences.zh: 但一直在流失的选民。

sentences.en: These coalitions that parties have relied on for decades are just way more movable than I think they had been.
sentences.zh: 政党几十年来所依赖的这些联盟，比我认为的要灵活得多。

sentences.en: Which gives both parties opportunities, but also has warning signs for both parties who were relying on voters to turn out and support them and are not reliably doing so
sentences.zh: 这既给了两党机会，也给两党敲响了警钟，因为他们依赖选民出来支持他们，但选民并没有以同样的方式

sentences.en: in the same ways.
sentences.zh: 可靠地这样做。

sentences.en: And I think what they won on the Democrats is really important, perhaps the most important thing.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为他们在民主党身上赢得了什么真的很重要，也许是最重要的事情。

sentences.en: Say more about that.
sentences.zh: 再多说一点。

sentences.en: Well, all three of the candidates in really the major races here, so governor of New Jersey, governor of Virginia, and mayor of New York City, which captured outside attention
sentences.zh: 嗯，这里所有三位在重大竞选中的候选人，即新泽西州州长、弗吉尼亚州州长和纽约市市长，这些竞选吸引了外界的关注，

sentences.en: as it is wont to do, ran on really these messages that were so focused on cost of living and affordability.
sentences.zh: 正如人们习惯的那样，他们所传达的信息非常关注生活成本和负担能力。

sentences.en: Like this was the my rent, housing, electricity, grocery, health care costs are all too damn high election.
sentences.zh: 就像这次选举的主题是：我的房租、住房、电费、杂货、医疗费用都太高了。

sentences.en: And they did that successfully.
sentences.zh: 而且他们成功地做到了这一点。

sentences.en: The reason why that is so unnerving for Republicans is traditionally economics have been a very strong point for the president.
sentences.zh: 共和党人感到不安的原因是，传统上经济一直是总统的强项。

sentences.en: People have thought that he would do a better job handling the economy than the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 人们一直认为他在处理经济问题上会比民主党人做得更好。

sentences.en: And we've really seen that edge erode to the point where Democrats were able to run a very successful campaign, almost exclusively focused on those issues, along with a heavy dose
sentences.zh: 我们确实看到这种优势被侵蚀，以至于民主党人能够开展一场非常成功的竞选活动，几乎完全专注于这些问题，再加上大量的

sentences.en: of, you know, opposition to the president, who's long been probably the best motivator for Democrats in the country.
sentences.zh: 反对总统的立场，他长期以来可能是全国民主党人最好的激励者。

sentences.en: And to your point, I had a conversation just before the election with Steve Bannon, one of President Trump's longtime advisors, who was very concerned about the president's
sentences.zh: 说到这一点，我在选举前刚与特朗普总统的长期顾问之一史蒂夫·班农谈过，他非常担心总统

sentences.en: hyper-focus on foreign policy.
sentences.zh: 对外交政策的过度关注。

sentences.en: He's meeting with foreign leaders multiple times a week.
sentences.zh: 他每周多次会见外国领导人。

sentences.en: He's done a lot of global travel.
sentences.zh: 他进行了大量的全球旅行。

sentences.en: He has not been traveling at all really domestically outside his homes in Florida and New Jersey.
sentences.zh: 他实际上根本没有在国内旅行，除了他在佛罗里达和新泽西的住所。

sentences.en: And some of the president's longtime advisors are saying you need to get back to focusing on the American people.
sentences.zh: 而总统的一些长期顾问说，你需要回到关注美国人民上来。

sentences.en: Well, why did the president take, and this is for all of you, why did the president take his eye off of the economy?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么总统，这是问你们所有人的，为什么总统把目光从经济上移开了？

sentences.en: It's not exactly news to him based on his presidential election victory a year ago that he won because of Americans' economic insecurities and their belief
sentences.zh: 根据一年前的总统大选胜利，他应该很清楚，他获胜是因为美国人的经济不安全感以及他们相信

sentences.en: that he was going to make life more affordable.
sentences.zh: 他会让生活变得更负担得起。

sentences.en: Well, but I think that he has focused on the economy in a lot of ways, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，但我认为他在很多方面都关注了经济，对吧？

sentences.en: We've talked about how he really leaned into tariffs and imposing tariffs on various countries, but he kept on making the case that that was going to help
sentences.zh: 我们谈到过他如何真正倾向于关税，并对各国征收关税，但他一直坚持认为这将有助于

sentences.en: Americans and help consumers and help manufacturing in this country.
sentences.zh: 美国人，有助于消费者，并有助于这个国家的制造业。

sentences.en: You look at the big tax cut bill that he spent a lot of political capital and a lot of time pushing through Congress earlier this year.
sentences.zh: 看看他今年早些时候花费了大量政治资本和大量时间推动国会通过的大型减税法案。

sentences.en: That was supposedly all about the economy.
sentences.zh: 那本应完全是关于经济的。

sentences.en: I think the problem has been that in doing all of those things, he has really seen a blowback.
sentences.zh: 我认为问题在于，在做所有这些事情的过程中，他确实看到了反弹。

sentences.en: Some of the tariffs have had negative effects on people in the United States.
sentences.zh: 一些关税对美国人民产生了负面影响。

sentences.en: Same thing on the tax bill.
sentences.zh: 税收法案也是如此。

sentences.en: In order to pay for that bill, they imposed massive Medicaid cuts.
sentences.zh: 为了支付该法案的费用，他们实施了大规模的医疗补助削减。

sentences.en: They cut nutritional benefits for Americans.
sentences.zh: 他们削减了美国人的营养福利。

sentences.en: And that was a calculated gamble that a tax cut was going to be politically positive for them.
sentences.zh: 这是一个经过计算的赌博，认为减税在政治上对他们有利。

sentences.en: But in the end, that did not help a big portion of his coalition.
sentences.zh: 但最终，这并没有帮助他联盟中的很大一部分人。

sentences.en: So I don't think it's that he hasn't been focused at all on the economy.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为并不是他根本没有关注经济。

sentences.en: It's just some of the impacts of what he has chosen to do are now just starting to be felt.
sentences.zh: 只是他所选择做的事情的一些影响现在才刚刚开始显现。

sentences.en: And Michael, just to add on to that, it's very reminiscent in some ways of Joe Biden's presidency.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，补充一点，这在某些方面非常让人想起乔·拜登的总统任期。

sentences.en: Because Joe Biden passed all this legislation and promised that the economy was going to get better but said that it would take time.
sentences.zh: 因为乔·拜登通过了所有这些立法，并承诺经济会好转，但表示这需要时间。

sentences.en: A lot of what Trump has done, he said, is in service of the economy.
sentences.zh: 特朗普所做的大部分事情，他说，都是为了经济服务。

sentences.en: The tariffs, as Julie said, the tax cut, trying to take stake of companies, saying he's bringing in all this business and investment into the United States.
sentences.zh: 正如朱莉所说，关税、减税，试图入股公司，说他正在将所有这些商业和投资引入美国。

sentences.en: But that is something that happens over a many-year period.
sentences.zh: 但这需要多年时间才能实现。

sentences.en: And I think that is a challenge for presidents who are stewarding an economy, is Americans want relief right now, and it's often hard to deliver that.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对管理经济的总统来说是一个挑战，因为美国人现在就想要救济，而这往往很难实现。

sentences.en: It's one thing, of course, for Democrats to have won races in blue places, right?
sentences.zh: 当然，民主党在蓝色地区赢得竞选是一回事，对吧？

sentences.en: New York City, blue.
sentences.zh: 纽约市，蓝色。

sentences.en: New Jersey, pretty blue.
sentences.zh: 新泽西州，相当蓝。

sentences.en: Virginia, pretty blue, although a little bit less than perhaps
sentences.zh: 弗吉尼亚州，相当蓝，尽管比

sentences.en: New Jersey and New York.
sentences.zh: 新泽西和纽约稍微少一点。

sentences.en: But Lisa Lear, I noticed these two races that nobody thought all that much about in Georgia,
sentences.zh: 但是丽莎·莱尔，我注意到佐治亚州那两场没人太在意的竞选，

sentences.en: statewide commission races,
sentences.zh: 全州委员会竞选，

sentences.en: where Democrats ousted Republicans by, like, the largest margins in decades.
sentences.zh: 民主党人以几十年来最大的优势将共和党人赶下台。

sentences.en: And if I'm the president,
sentences.zh: 如果我是总统，

sentences.en: that would really worry me.
sentences.zh: 那真的会让我担心。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think the scale of the Democratic wins here is really important, as you're pointing out.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为民主党在这里获胜的规模非常重要，正如你指出的那样。

sentences.en: We sort of, it was widely expected in the newsroom, we anticipated that Democrats would win those three major races that we've talked about.
sentences.zh: 我们有点，新闻编辑室里普遍预期，我们预料到民主党会赢得我们谈到的那三场重大竞选。

sentences.en: But it was these lower races.
sentences.zh: 但这些较小的竞选才是关键。

sentences.en: They made huge gains in the Virginia Statehouse.
sentences.zh: 他们在弗吉尼亚州议会取得了巨大进展。

sentences.en: They won these two
sentences.zh: 他们赢得了这两场

sentences.en: Georgia Utility Board races, which, you know, I talked to Republicans there and they said, well, we weren't paying attention to this, we weren't invested in it.
sentences.zh: 佐治亚州公用事业委员会竞选，你知道，我和那里的共和党人谈过，他们说，嗯，我们没关注这个，我们没投入精力。

sentences.en: But, you know,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，

sentences.en: Democrats still flipped those seats and the margins were really high.
sentences.zh: 民主党人还是翻转了这些席位，而且优势非常大。

sentences.en: It shows that the energy is still there and it shows that
sentences.zh: 这表明能量依然存在，也表明

sentences.en: Republicans haven't solved one of their most sort of pernicious problems, which is their inability to get their voters to turn out when Donald Trump's name is not on the ballot.
